records.text: Candace Owens offered 10,000 dollars and source protection to anyone who provides opposite-side footage showing who recorded Erika Kirk leaving the White House correspondents event
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I'll put a bounty on it. I will. offer $10,000 to somebody who has the opposite side footage. ... And I obviously will not run your name. I will protect you. If you have that opposite side footage of the person who caught that footage, 10K is yours, no questions asked.

verification.notes: The primary source episode records Owens offering 10,000 dollars, anonymity, and source protection to anyone providing opposite-side footage showing who recorded Erika Kirk leaving. This verifies the offer; no claim of payout or fulfillment is made.

records.text: Candace Owens said Sara Sidner did not respond to repeated requests to confirm whether Sidner personally recorded the footage of Erika Kirk leaving the correspondents event
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And so I reached out to her on Instagram ahead of this show. ... I reached out yesterday and I think the day before on Instagram, on Twitter and via text asking her to simply confirm that she in fact shot the video and that it was not given to her by somebody else. ... I got no response.

verification.notes: CNN confirms Sidner reported on the Erika Kirk footage, but Owens alleged outreach through Instagram, X, and private text is not publicly auditable. No reliable source confirms the messages were received or that Sidner failed to respond.

records.text: Candace Owens said she believed Sara Sidner probably received the Erika Kirk video from someone else before posting it rather than recording it herself
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I didn't buy that Sara Sidner of CNN, who initially put the video online, recorded it. She stopped short of saying that she recorded it. ... I felt that she likely had that video sent to her.

links.title: Sidner May Have Received, Not Recorded, Clip

records.text: Sara Sidner was the first person to post Erika Kirk's “I want to go home” video on social media, uploading it to Instagram at 9:25 p.m. Eastern.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Then at 9.25 p.m., so a little under an hour later, Sara Sidner, you will recall of CNN, she became the first person on. ... on social media to upload the now infamous I want to go home video of Erika Kirk. ... She posted it onto Instagram. ... That is 9.25 p.m. Eastern time, okay?

verification.notes: Context shows Owens relied on displayed Instagram metadata. Current reporting confirms Sidner posted the clip, and the transcript metadata supports 9:25 p.m. Eastern, but no reliable public record establishes that she was the first person on all social media to publish it.

records.text: The Erika Kirk video was not recorded by Sara Sidner; it was distributed to Sidner after operatives recorded the moment.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep 7FS1tUeSfdE)

appearances.snippet: I told you I am told that this was not a video recorded by Sara Sidner and that instead it was distributed to Sara Sidner and that they had operatives record that moment.

verification.notes: The transcript attributes this to an anonymous source. Current coverage confirms Sidner posted the video and records Owens allegation that it was sent to her, but no identified recorder, original file provenance, or independent witness establishes who recorded or distributed it.
